events.title: Music for Action, a Climate Week Concert: Young the Giant / St. Lucia / DREEEMY DJ Set
events.description:
Turning up the Volume on Climate Change & Tick-Borne Disease: This show  is raising awareness about climate change and the resulting increase in tick-borne diseases, including in urban areas and city parks. Concert-goers will leave equipped to stay safe while enjoying the outdoors. 
  Performing for the evening is multi-platinum Southern California rock band   Young the Giant  , known for their hit songs like “Cough Syrup” and “My Body.” Their sixth full-length album,    Victory Garden   , explores themes of resilience and connection, culminating their years of advocacy and music. The group has made environmental action a priority on the road, partnering with environmental nonprofit REVERB to reduce the impact of its tours by calculating its tour-related carbon footprint, supporting local climate and social nonprofits in the communities it visits, and contributing a portion of ticket proceeds to REVERB’s Climate Project Portfolio. Joining the bill is Jean-Philip Grobler and Patti Beranek’s alt-pop project   St. Lucia  , performing work from their album    Dusk   . DREEEMY will kick off the evening with a DJ set.   
  For a chance to win VIP tickets to Music for Action, a Climate Week Concert, you can RSVP for the show  here , although as all SummerStage shows, this one remains free, first come, first served until we fill up. RSVP is  not required  to attend this show and does not guarantee entry.

events.title: Of Monsters and Men / August Ponthier
events.description: The Icelandic indie band broke onto the scene in 2011 with their hit “Little Talks,” which led to more than a billion Spotify streams and a    Saturday Night Live    performance. Since then, they’ve run the gamut of performance from cameos on    HBO   ’s    Game of Thrones    to sets at Coachella, Glastonbury, and Lollapalooza. After some time pursuing solo projects, they’re reuniting for The Mouse Parade Tour, named for their most recent 2025 album. Indie singer songwriter August Ponthier will open the evening.

events.title: The Age of the Ram Tour: Charley Crockett with special guests Durand Jones and the Indications / Honky Tonkin’ in Queens
events.description:
SummerStage Member  Presale:  Thursday, March 5 at 12PM  
  Capital One Cardholder  Presale:  Tuesday, March 3 at 11AM   
 General on-sale:  Friday, March 6 at 10AM  
 “Street busker turned critically acclaimed singer-songwriter turned actual country star” ( Rolling   Stone ), Charley Crockett’s particular brand of country has earned him millions of streams and several GRAMMY nominations. His deep voice and Americana style on songs like “Lonesome Drifter” and “I’m Just a Clown” evoke a version of the country filled with tumbleweeds and cowboys. He’s played across the U.S. at venues including Red Rocks, the Hollywood Bowl, and even SummerStage in 2022, when he opened for Willie Nelson. Durand Jones and the Indications will open the evening. 
  Charley Crockett, in partnership with PLUS1, will contribute $1.00 from every ticket sold to Last Prisoner Project.

events.title: Odd Mob
events.description:
Due to Friday’s extreme heat threat (temps expected over 100°), the Odd Mob performance in Central Park on 7/3 has been rescheduled to 5/29/2027 . More information can be found at your point of purchase.  
  Known for his genre-defying approach, Australian producer and DJ   Odd Mob   has cemented his place at the forefront of global electronic music. He broke through with the 2014 hit ‘Is It A Banger’; since then, Odd Mob has released a string of hits like ‘LEFT TO RIGHT,’ ‘Get Busy,’ and many more, pushing him past 400+ million streams across platforms. 2026 is looking to be his biggest year yet with a string of new releases and shows across the U.S.A, Asia, Europe, the U.K., and in his home region of Australia.
